findings.title: retryCount incremented via stale read-modify-write instead of atomic increment
findings.body: Both failure paths set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched at the start of the run. If two cron executions overlap (or the row is otherwise updated between the findMany and the update), one increment is lost, so a reminder that should be deleted after two failures survives for extra runs. Prisma supports `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`, which is atomic and immune to the stale read; it should be used in both the `else` branch (line ~184) and the `catch` block (line ~195).

findings.title: Unguarded retryCount update in catch block can crash the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch handler now performs `prisma.workflowReminder.update` before logging. If that update itself throws (e.g., the database error that caused the original exception persists, or the row was concurrently deleted), the exception propagates out of the for-loop, the handler returns a 500, and all remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are skipped for this run. The update in the catch block should be wrapped in its own try/catch (or the failure recorded without a second awaited DB call) so one failing reminder cannot abort processing of the rest.

findings.title: retryCount-based deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the deleteMany has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the sibling branch. WorkflowReminder rows are shared across EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP methods, so any non-SMS reminder that ever gets retryCount > 1 (e.g., if the email cron adopts the same retry pattern, or via manual/data-fix updates) will be silently deleted by the SMS cron. The method filter should be applied to the whole OR (or duplicated in the retryCount branch) to keep this cron from touching other reminder types.
